mission.title: A Plethora of Passwords
mission.description: Download the Ouroboros Corporation's password file and start putting it to use before the Agents catch on.

npc.say: Tch. They're all at a "leadership training seminar." Apparently, it tells them how to take advantage of their higher salaries.
It's true! I falsified those deductions! Oh, god!

phase.briefing: Ookami managed to pull some information about Ouroboros' network from the employee you absconded with last week, operative. Now we'll see if it's actually "legit." A terminal in the indicated Ouroboros Corporation office is supposed to have a means of downloading a file containing passwords to many of their systems.

enter.say: Some low-level signals in there. If they've got security, they must be taking a siesta.

done.say: Ahh, what the smeg? Just lost connection to the server. We're gonna have to go find the damn box ourselves.

near.say: No, still no reception. Dang it, we've probably missed the whole first inning! What'd they do, put lead shielding in the walls here?

phase.briefing:
No, operative, we won't let the mean old FTP server get away with being rude to you like that.
God, I could do this faster myself with a command line. Why do I keep paying these people... Hm? Oh. Damn speakerpho--

enter.say: Trace from the brief connection gave me that building as the server's location. All I'm picking up right now is some computer and network activity.
Looks like something caused the server to power cycle while we were connected. We should be able to bring it back up from the mainframe there.

done.say: Okay, the server's back up. Let's get that password data.

objective.text: Get the Data from the Computer

done.say:
Ah, nothing like a batch of passwords to other people's stuff. Upload that to me at a hardli--
Ooh, I think security just showed up. Careful on your way out.
Clearance is not required. This is a federal investigation. If you have questions, contact your liaison in the bureau.

phase.briefing: So many passwords, so little time... Now we just have to see what we can get with them. Even if whatever they have that's related to the "Oligarch Network" in the no-fly zone turns out to be worthless, a large company like that is bound to have quite a bit of valuable information just waiting to be sold at fair black market prices.

enter.say: I think we ditched 'em for now... Just get to a terminal, and we'll start plugging away with the passwords we got from that file.

done.say:
Hm. Well, that's promising. Why don't you try--
Uh-oh, those signals are seriously incoming now. ... Hell, I think some of those are Machines. We're gonna have to cut this short.

near.say: Tch. They're all at a "leadership training seminar." Apparently, it tells them how to take advantage of their higher salaries.
Better hurry; I don't like the look of these incoming signals I'm picking up...

phase.briefing:
For pity's sake, operative; first you attract a Cypherite spy, and now it's full-fledged Machines. How are we supposed to get any work done when you're irresistible to G-men?
No accounting for taste...

enter.say: Okay, I have an idea on exactly what we can try searching for this time. We'll be in and out before they can catch up to us. No prob.

talk.say:
Hello, Ms. Napilitano. I'm afraid that we can't permit this to continue.
Oh, I realize it would be pointless to arrest you. This is merely a warning: cease your activity at the Ouroboros Corporation, or we will be forced to take...measures.

done.say: I will leave that to your imagination, Ms. Napilitano.

near.say: Should just be in the next-- Gah!

mission.finish:
...
There's more than one way to recycle a toaster, Ms. Napilitano: a socket and a bathtub, for instance; the gentle caress of a sledgehammer, or fooling them into dividing by zero.
It's a big network out there, operative. They can stop you, but not us.
